# DeepWork

> DeepWork is a free, local-first focus timer, task manager and habit tracker for
> Windows, macOS, Linux and the web. It keeps every task, focus session, journal
> entry and habit in a database on the user's own machine: no account, no cloud
> sync, no telemetry on the user's work and no subscription. The web build at
> https://app.deepwork.rajatmalik.dev/ is the same application, installable as a PWA.

This file describes the web app. The product page, with screenshots and the full
marketing copy, is https://deepwork.rajatmalik.dev/ (its own guide is
https://deepwork.rajatmalik.dev/llms.txt).

## Key facts

- **Price:** free. No paid tier, trial, account or card.
- **Version described here:** 3.0.3.
- **Platforms:** Windows 10+, macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon), Linux
  (.AppImage/.deb/.rpm) and any modern browser. There is no native iOS or
  Android app.
- **Storage:** a local SQLite file (`deepwork.db`) in the desktop app; browser
  `localStorage` in the web build. Clearing site data in a browser erases it, so
  the app offers a JSON backup export and import.
- **Network:** the desktop app contacts the public GitHub releases API to check
  for updates, downloads an installer only when the user presses Update, and
  opens links the user clicks. The web build additionally uses an opt-out
  GoatCounter visit counter that sends the page path and title, never a task, a
  journal entry or an identifier.
- **Licence:** MIT - https://github.com/malikrajat/deepwork/blob/main/LICENSE
- **Repository:** https://github.com/malikrajat/deepwork
- **Downloads:** https://github.com/malikrajat/deepwork/releases/latest

## What it does

- **Focus timer:** Pomodoro-style focus sessions with short and long breaks,
  configurable lengths, an animated ring, completion alerts that repeat until
  answered, and a twelve-colour cycle.
- **Tasks:** a status board (To Do / In Progress / Done) filed into date
  sections, an Eisenhower matrix, and a Today view. Add, edit, search, sort,
  import from Excel/CSV (with a validated preview) and export to CSV.
- **Calendar:** queues tasks into focus blocks across a day timeline.
- **Time by Task:** every focus session grouped by the work it paid for, with
  all-time totals, first and last session, a repeat rhythm, and a custom range.
- **Reminders:** stored reminders that survive a restart and keep asking until
  Done, Snooze or Stop, with matching desktop notifications.
- **Habits and journal:** daily habits with streaks, and dated journal entries
  with word counts and a writing-versus-focus correlation.
- **Analytics:** focus, task, habit and journal figures with trends and streaks,
  each paired with a plain-language reading. These readings are deterministic
  rules and totals built into the app; DeepWork contains no AI model and makes
  no inference calls.
- **Desktop behaviour:** system tray, start with system, always on top, and a
  small always-on-top timer widget.

## Pages

- `/` - dashboard: the focus timer, today's tasks, the session cycle.
- `/tasks` - the task board and list.
- `/matrix` - the Eisenhower matrix.
- `/calendar` - the day planner.
- `/today` - everything due today.
- `/analytics` - figures and their readings.
- `/time` - Time by Task reporting.
- `/reminders` - standing reminders.
- `/habits` - habits and streaks.
- `/journal` - dated journal entries.
- `/settings` - timer, notifications, backup and diagnostics.
- `/about` - who builds it, version, update check, downloads.
- `/contact` - how to reach the developer.
- `/privacy` and `/terms` - the policies.

The workspace pages are rendered from the visitor's own local data, so a crawler
sees the application shell rather than any personal content.

## How to use it

Open https://app.deepwork.rajatmalik.dev/ and start a focus session; nothing has
to be installed or signed up for. For an installable version, use the browser's
install prompt or download a desktop build from the releases page. The desktop
build is the one with a real SQLite database and a tray; the web build keeps its
data in browser storage.

## Limitations, stated plainly

- No cloud or multi-device sync; each machine has its own database.
- No team, sharing or collaboration features.
- No native mobile app.
- The desktop installers are unsigned, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS
  Gatekeeper warn on first launch.
